artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth connected Riemannian manifold. Call $(M,g)$ locally homogeneous if for every pair of points $p,q\in M$ there exist open neighborhoods $U\ni p$, $V\ni q$ and an isometry $\varphi:(U,g|_U)\to(V,g|_V)$ with $\varphi(p)=q$. Call $(M,g)$ $1$-homogeneous if for every pair of points $p,q\in M$ there exists a local isometry between neighborhoods of $p$ and $q$ matching the metric and its first covariant derivatives at the basepoints; equivalently (in terms of geodesic flow), there exist linear-in-momenta first integrals of the geodesic flow whose values at each point of $M$ span the tangent space.

Question: Must every $1$-homogeneous Riemannian manifold be locally homogeneous?

It is known that the answer is affirmative in dimensions $3$ and $4$, while the analogous statement fails for indefinite (pseudo-Riemannian) metrics. Determine whether the implication "$1$-homogeneous $\Rightarrow$ locally homogeneous" holds for Riemannian manifolds of all dimensions.
artifact.status_search_result: No source was found resolving the conjecture in general dimensions. Results were established affirmatively for dimensions 3 and 4, and counterexamples exist in pseudo-Riemannian signature, but the general Riemannian case appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Homothety Homogeneity and Local Homogeneity
status_evidence.snippet: Work by García-Río, Gilkey and Nikčević focused on homothety homogeneity and local homogeneity.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between forms of homogeneity and local homogeneity remains an active topic with no general affirmative resolution cited.

status_evidence.title: Curvature Homogeneous Pseudo-Riemannian Manifolds which are not Locally Homogeneous
status_evidence.snippet: There exist balanced signature pseudo-Riemannian manifolds which are curvature homogeneous and not locally homogeneous.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples are known in pseudo-Riemannian signature, consistent with the problem's note.
